correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed all 35 tetrahedra from four cyclic representatives, with f-vector (10,45,70,35), a complete graph as 1-skeleton, and exactly 70 facial/50 missing triangles. Spanning-tree collapse reduces ∂2 to 70x36 integral cycle relation matrix R with rank 35. Source verifier supplies a 35x35 unimodular minor of determinant -1 and primitive annihilating cocycle, proving H1=Z with no torsion, not merely rational rank one. Independently recomputed the primitive annihilator and evaluated all 50 missing triangles: value distribution +1:30,-1:10,0:10, with 5 cyclic orbits of size 10. Independent apex enumeration yields (0,3) for exactly 10 null triangles and (±1,0) for the other 40; representative (1,2,8) has apices 3,6,7. These finite exhaustive checks cover all faces/triangles/apices of the specified complex; no infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: On a canonical neighborly S2×S1 triangulation, the exact integral homology classes of all shortest nonfacial 3-cycles and their local conical fillability classify a natural minimum-support invariant, giving a concrete local criterion for null-homologous shortest cycles. This is object-specific but complete, reproducible and mathematically motivated beyond restating a facet table.
residual_risks: No universal classification of all neighborly manifold triangulations or geometric systolic metric claim follows.

final_claim: In cyclic neighborly ten-vertex S^2×S^1 triangulation generated by facet C10-orbit representatives 1236,1237,1257,1368 (latter half orbit), the 50 empty triangles split into 40 primitive nonzero integral H1 classes and one null orbit of size 10; exactly the 10 null triangles admit a three-face cone disk, each with exactly 3 possible apices.
limitations: Finite natural object-specific homology shell; not a general manifold theorem.
Exact computations only for specified cyclic 10-vertex simplicial model.
